title: Not Open for Business

object.label: US control of the Strait of Hormuz (H6, proposed) — throughput as control

transformNote: CENTCOM's 'open under US control' (10-12) read against its own falsifier: H6 falls if a commercial vessel is sunk or disabled in the Strait within 14 days of 10-15. scoreboard.zRule: every line carries a z, inferred where implied (Sailor 2026-10-13); inferred lines are marked zInferred with a zWhy

lines.quote: Sea mine crisis re-emerges in Strait of Hormuz as Tehran urges Washington to accept deal
lines.note: THE DOOR: 'crisis' is the vehicle, 're-emerges' dates it (the mines were cleared once — the headline's own link), 'urges' puts the deal in Tehran's hands
lines.zWhy: a re-emerging mine crisis is not a controlled strait

lines.quote: Iran claimed Oct. 17 that two oil tankers caught fire after striking mines in the Strait
lines.note: THE FALSIFIER'S SIGHTING: H6 falls on a commercial vessel sunk or disabled within 14 days of 10-15. Two days in, by the adversary's claim. Verify: a hull name, an insurer, Kpler
lines.zWhy: two tankers burning on mines reads against control, if the claim holds

lines.quote: the IMO warned mines pose a serious threat to vessels; Tehran keeps its own unauthorized shipping corridor inside its territorial waters
lines.note: two routes on one strait: the regulator's and Iran's. 'Unauthorized' is Fox's word for Iran's corridor; Iran's word for the IMO route is the same (¶7)
lines.zWhy: a strait with two competing routes is priced by whoever holds the safe one

lines.quote: the information we have is that they still have mines in the traffic separation scheme; while the conflict is ongoing it is very difficult to use third parties to verify
lines.note: THE INSTRUMENT'S OWN BLINDNESS: the regulator says it cannot verify the record — the horizon named by the body that keeps the chart
lines.zWhy: an unverifiable minefield on the recognized route is not control

lines.quote: we cannot guarantee that a vessel intending to transit that route will not be hit by a mine
lines.note: the mechanism: no guarantee → no insurance → no passage at the old price (L2-toll-2's freight line, from the regulator's side)
lines.zWhy: a passage no one can guarantee is a passage priced by risk

lines.quote: both tankers were reportedly carrying about 2 million barrels of crude
lines.note: the cargo sized — a tenth of CENTCOM's daily count, on two hulls
lines.zWhy: two million barrels stopped is throughput lost

lines.quote: the ships allegedly turned off positioning and radar and used a route Iran had not authorized
lines.note: IRAN'S FRAME: the hit as the ship's fault for refusing the toll road. Who authorizes passage is the object itself, stated from the other side
lines.zWhy: a strait where Iran authorizes the route is Iran's to price

lines.quote: the second tanker was left immobilized after hitting a mine (Reuters)
lines.note: THE FALSIFIER'S TERM: 'disabled' is H6's word; 'immobilized' is the wire's. The lowest-Dia line in the cut
lines.zWhy: a hull immobilized in the Strait is the falsifier, literally

lines.quote: Tehran's passage inside its waters charges IRGC-administered tolls and fees, which Washington and the IMO reject
lines.note: L2-toll-1 (Krystal, 10-15: countries are paying Iran for passage) now stated from the RI corner, as a fact the US 'rejects' — rejecting a toll is not the same as not paying it
lines.zWhy: a tolled corridor is passage priced by Iran

lines.quote: the one transit route is not safe, because mines remain on it
lines.note: the recognized route (1968) declared unsafe by its keeper
lines.zWhy: the only lawful route unsafe is the Strait closed in law

lines.quote: the IMO has confirmation of Iran's temporary route but has not approved it; any other route must come to the organization for review
lines.note: the status of Iran's corridor, exactly: confirmed, unapproved, unreviewed
lines.zWhy: an unapproved corridor in use is a fact on the water, not on the chart

lines.quote: amid stalled US–Iran talks on ending the conflict and restoring shipping
lines.note: 'restoring shipping' concedes shipping is not restored — the article's own Z, in passing
lines.zWhy: shipping still to be restored is not shipping under control

lines.quote: Washington's latest response is insufficient; the US accepted some of Iran's seven conditions; Tehran has stopped responding
lines.note: the adversary's frame on the talks; 'seven conditions' is the only sized thing in it. The hottest line in the cut
lines.zWhy: a counterparty that stops responding holds the pace

lines.quote: Iran sent a proposal through Qatar: the Strait could reopen and traffic resume within seven days
lines.note: THE COUNTER-OBJECT: 'could reopen' concedes closed. The Z-assertion read backwards from Tehran — the Strait's opening offered as Iran's to give, on a seven-day clock
lines.zWhy: a reopening offered by Iran is a strait Iran holds

lines.quote: attacks on commercial vessels around Hormuz have surged over the past two weeks
lines.note: the rate, undated and uncounted (BP 10-16 had 'a couple a day'; NYT 10-15 had 26 in October)
lines.zWhy: a surging attack rate is the loss-rate reading, from RI

lines.quote: senior Iranian officials told Reuters Tehran has changed its tactics for attacking commercial ships in that period
lines.note: the adversary's own admission of the rate — a detection-series row (tactics changed, ≈10-06 → 10-20)
lines.zWhy: an adversary announcing new tactics is not deterred

lines.quote: not open for business in the way that it was before the conflict started
lines.note: THE RECORD LINE: the regulator reads H6 in H6's own word — 'open' — and says not. The title
lines.zWhy: not open as before is the object stated, from the chart's keeper

lines.quote: the IMO is preparing to resume operations, but not until the root causes are addressed
lines.note: the regulator's own window: open when the conflict ends, not before
lines.zWhy: a resumption conditioned on the war's end is a strait closed for the war's length

lines.quote: Fox News Digital contacted CENTCOM for comment; no response
lines.note: THE CHALLENGE, BY ABSENCE: H6's principal asked about its own assertion and silent. The line the cut turns on
lines.zWhy: a principal that does not answer does not restate the count
